comment: What host64 adds to the game, and which client builds each addition works on. tools/buildinfo.py resolves this for the build tools/prepare.py chose: generated/build.h gets FFXI_FEATURE_<ID> 1 or 0 and FFXI_FEATURE_TABLE (host64 --features prints it as JSON), and runtime.json beside a build lists each feature with whether it is on and why not, for the launcher. A feature is on for a build when every rule holds: min_build / max_build (build labels, the PE timestamp dates recomp/meta/builds.json is keyed by, compared as text), builds (only these labels) and needs (keys the build's recomp/meta/builds.json entry must have: 'hooks.lod_pick', 'patches.frame60', 'addresses.scene_mgr', or 'modern' for a complete Config > Modern address set). A build's own entry can override the result with "features": {"<id>": true} (on despite the rules, tested) or {"<id>": "<why it is off>"}. Where the code also checks a build's hooks at compile time (#if defined(FFXI_HOOK_...)), needs repeats the main ones so the launcher can say why; both must hold. A feature the catalog leaves out is not gated.

aspect.title: Widescreen 3D view
aspect.what: The scene's aspect ratio follows the window (--aspect). The camera field is read from the game's own setter, so it is safe on every build.

draw_distance.title: Draw distance
draw_distance.what: Scales the world's and characters' draw distance (--draw-distance, fx draw / draw_entities), through the globals Ashita's drawdistance addon finds.

frame_divisor.title: Frame rate (30 / 60)
frame_divisor.what: Sets the game's frame divisor (--fps-divisor, Config > Display > Frame Rate). Clients from 2025 on keep one; older ones have none and use frame60.

frame60.title: 60 fps (code patch)
frame60.what: For clients with no frame divisor: a translated variant of the frame loop that waits for and steps the world by one sixtieth instead of two, switched on in the world with --fps-divisor 1 (the title and lobby count frames for 30 and stay there).

uncapped.title: Uncapped frame rate (120 / 144 / unlimited)
uncapped.what: Frame pacing past 60 with the world kept at its speed.

nameplates.title: Nameplate shape and size
nameplates.what: Keeps the names over characters' heads at their 4:3 shape and scales them (--nameplates, --nameplate-scale).

lod.title: Near models at every distance
lod.what: Picks the near level of detail for every model (--lod near). Reads the model objects at today's offsets.

water.title: Modern water
water.what: Marks the zone's water models so the effects draw them as water (fx water).

scene.title: Scene renderer (sun shadows, lamps, modern fog)
scene.what: Reads the zone's lights, fog and models from the game's own structures (fx scene).

sun_prime.title: Shadows from behind the camera
sun_prime.what: Lets the map renderer draw what is out of view once, for the sun's shadow map.

modern_menus.title: Config > Modern and Config > Menus
modern_menus.what: The in-game settings menus host64 adds.

cexi.title: Custom items (CatsEyeXI)
cexi.what: A custom server's own items, gear sets and spells (--cexi).

addons.title: Addons (Ashita, Windower, xi)
addons.what: Loads the player's Lua addons and their startup scripts. Ashita's and Windower's libraries, resources and packet layouts are today's: on older clients addons misread the packets and print wrong names (battlemod's action messages), so they are not loaded. The addon host itself still runs for the host's own parts (the control port, the 60 fps login check).

dinput_pad.title: Gamepad map on DirectInput-only clients
dinput_pad.what: For clients that read the gamepad only through DirectInput (no XInput; the 2009 one), the pad's buttons are numbered as the game's XInput codes are, the triggers and the D-pad as buttons too, so padsin000 (ffxi.reg's map, Config > Gamepad's) means the same buttons as on today's clients. Without it the shipped map is scrambled there: Confirm on Y, Cancel on A, the menus on Back, Start and the shoulders.

modern_fx.title: Modern effects (post-processing)
modern_fx.what: Grading, saturation, contrast, sharpening and anisotropic filtering over the game's own picture. Works on the finished frame, not the game's data, so every build has it.

ps2_draws.title: PS2 Accuracy (draws)
ps2_draws.what: Draws what the PC version got wrong as the PS2 does: metal's shine, summons' halos, Port Bastok's sea, menu buttons (fix_ps2). Works on the game's draws, not its code, so needs no hooks; tested on 2025 and 2026 builds.

ps2_models.title: PS2 Accuracy (shine batches, disintegrate)
ps2_models.what: The shine batches the PC's weapon files lost, and the Shadow Lord's break-up (fix_shine, fix_disintegrate), through the skinning call and the particle op dispatch.
